profile.campus: QTS Phoenix 2 (PHX2), 1200 to 1500 North 40th Street, Phoenix, Arizona
profile.reading:
The building mapped here is one of the five data centres on QTS Phoenix 2, a campus that runs along the west side of North 40th Street between McDowell Road and the Loop 202 Red Mountain Freeway, in the Camelback East village of Phoenix. Maricopa County parcel records resolve exactly which building it is. Assessor parcel 121-01-640, whose boundary contains this record's coordinates, carries the situs address 1500 North 40th Street, Phoenix, Arizona 85008, is classified under the county's data centre property use code, and is owned by QTS Phoenix II DC5 LLC, a single purpose entity whose mailing address is 6601 College Boulevard, Overland Park, Kansas, the head office of QTS itself. The county records the parcel at 18.61 acres, two storeys, and a construction year of 2024. Its deed was recorded in February 2024. An earlier version of this registry entry carried an address on East McDowell Road that reverse geocoding had attached to an apartment complex more than a mile away. That address was wrong and has been replaced with the county's.

QTS, originally Quality Technology Services, was founded in 2003, is headquartered in Overland Park, Kansas, and was taken private by Blackstone in 2021. The five buildings sit on sibling parcels in a single recorded subdivision the county names McDowell Road Data Center Phase 2, all of them inside the Creighton Elementary School District and Phoenix Union High School District 210. The county lists 1200 North 40th Street as DC1 on 12.92 acres with a construction year of 2022, then 1250 as DC2 on 11.48 acres, 1400 as DC3 on 13.06 acres, 1450 as DC4 on 12.53 acres and this parcel as DC5, the last four all dated 2024. Three further parcels in the same subdivision, of 10.44, 3.44 and 1.27 acres, are still carried as vacant. The eight parcels together come to about 83.7 acres, which squares with the roughly 80 acre campus QTS describes.

The land came to this use through a rezoning rather than by sitting idle in an industrial district. In December 2017 the Phoenix Planning Commission heard case Z-62-17-8, the McDowell Road Data Center PUD, which converted 97.85 acres from a patchwork of seven residential and commercial districts, including single family R1-6 covering 25.05 acres, into one planned unit development. Staff described the site as vacant with minimal native vegetation and recommended approval subject to 44 stipulations. Those conditions include a minimum 60 foot building setback from perimeter lot lines, a maximum height of 85 feet reached only beyond 100 feet from the perimeter, and a 100 foot setback for utility equipment yards, loading docks and trash areas from residentially zoned property.

What is not known here matters as much as what is. QTS publishes 210 MW and more of critical campus capacity for the whole five building campus and gives no figure for any single building, so no IT load is recorded for this row. The county carries no building square footage for the parcel. The tenant is not public.

profile.capacity_note: QTS publishes 210 MW and more of critical campus capacity for the whole five building Phoenix 2 campus. That is a campus figure and QTS calls it critical capacity, not IT load, so no it_capacity_mw is recorded for this building. Data Center Dynamics separately reported 1200 North 40th Street at 337,330 square feet and 42 MW, which is DC1, a different building on the same campus and not this one. No utility service figure and no standby generation figure are published for any building here, so those keys are absent too.
profile.facility_note: QTS Phoenix 2 DC5, confirmed by Maricopa County assessor parcel 121-01-640, owner QTS Phoenix II DC5 LLC, situs 1500 North 40th Street, Phoenix AZ 85008, construction year 2024, 18.61 acres.
profile.research_note: Resolved 2026-09-05. The prior entry treated this as an unidentifiable QTS point at a reverse geocoded apartment address on East McDowell Road. Maricopa County GIS parcel query at the stored coordinates returns parcel 121-01-640, owner QTS Phoenix II DC5 LLC, situs 1500 North 40th Street, subdivision McDowell Road Data Center Phase 2, use code 1507 data centers. The building is QTS Phoenix 2 DC5. No per building power figure exists in any primary source, so none is stored.
profile.community_note: What the City of Phoenix decided about data centres is on the public record twice, eight years apart, and this campus sits between the two decisions. In December 2017 the Planning Commission heard case Z-62-17-8 and converted 97.85 acres at 40th Street and McDowell Road, including 25.05 acres of single family R1-6 and 21.79 acres of neighbourhood shopping centre zoning, into one planned unit development for a data centre campus, commerce park and open space. Staff recommended approval with 44 stipulations and recorded no neighbourhood opposition in the report. In 2025 the city went back and wrote general rules. Text amendment Z-TA-2-25-Y was heard on 1 May 2025 and adopted by the Mayor and Council on 2 July 2025, and the city described its purpose as addressing power grid reliability, fire risk, emergency response access and noise impacts as data centre growth accelerated. The parcel lies in taxing district 141300, Creighton School District in the City of Phoenix, so the Creighton Elementary School District and Phoenix Union High School District 210 receive shares of the property tax on it without any abatement appearing in the county record.
profile.incentives_note: No abatement appears in the county record for this parcel. For tax year 2025 Maricopa County records a full cash value of $105,226,836 on parcel 121-01-640, of which $92,565,836 is improvements and $12,661,000 is land, and a full assessed property tax of $862,623.16, including $80,838.88 of city tax. The parcel sits in taxing district 141300, Creighton School District in the City of Phoenix, so the Creighton Elementary School District and Phoenix Union High School District 210 are among the recipients. Sibling parcels on the same campus carry comparable bills, including $894,167.84 at 1400 North 40th Street and $716,654.66 at 1250 North 40th Street.
profile.regulatory_note: Siting jurisdiction is the City of Phoenix. The campus land was rezoned to a planned unit development in December 2017 under case Z-62-17-8, the McDowell Road Data Center PUD, covering 97.85 acres with 44 stipulations, a 60 foot minimum perimeter building setback, an 85 foot height maximum with stepbacks, and a 100 foot setback for utility yards, loading docks and trash areas from residential zoning. Phoenix did not define data centres in its zoning ordinance at all until text amendment Z-TA-2-25-Y, which the Mayor and Council adopted on 2 July 2025. That amendment permits data centres only in the C-2, C-3, CP/GCP, A-1 and A-2 districts and only with a Special Permit, requires all mechanical equipment to sit at least 150 feet from abutting right of way or residentially zoned property, bars development closer than 2,640 feet to an approved high capacity transit station, caps noise at 5 percent above measured ambient for sites within 300 feet of residential zoning with a third party acoustical study required, and conditions preliminary approval on a utility will serve letter confirming the energy demand can be served within two years. This campus was entitled almost eight years before those standards existed.
profile.regional_context: QTS was founded 2003 by Chad Williams, HQ Overland Park KS, IPO 2013, acquired by Blackstone (BREIT) for ~$10B, completed August 31 2021.
profile.campus_power_note: The five Phoenix 2 buildings share a campus electrical and fibre spine, and QTS describes a redundant campus fibre conduit system linking them. Axios Phoenix reported in August 2022 that Salt River Project was building a power substation on the property. SRP is the electric utility for the campus. SRP states that data centres contributed 5.1 percent of its record summer 2025 peak demand, that its generation capacity is about 8,000 MW, and that some of the larger data centres on its system carry a load of 200 MW. Its E-67 price plan, approved in 2025, applies to commercial and industrial customers with 20 MW or more of forecast load and sets minimum billing at the greater of actual demand or 80 percent of forecast load.
profile.campus_mapped_here: OpenStreetMap carries data centre footprints for two of the five QTS Phoenix 2 buildings. This record is the northern one, way 1315636714 at parcel 121-01-640. Way 1132632705, about a quarter mile south, is the other.

reading.body:
This record maps to a McDowell Road address in Phoenix that does not match any of QTS's confirmed current facilities in the metro area, which the operator lists as PHX1, PHX2, PHX3, PHX4, and Avondale. No independent confirmation of a QTS presence at this address exists. The record may reflect a mapping error, an outdated or closed location, or a site not yet covered by QTS's public materials.

QTS publishes no specifications for this mapped point, so no capacity, power allocation, or configuration can be stated. Arizona has 56 mapped data center facilities of which only four publish power figures, totaling 512 MW. Without confirmed specs, this campus cannot be ranked against the state's published capacity.

This campus does not appear in current QTS public listings and carries no verified specifications. It does not factor into decisions about AI infrastructure scaling in Arizona or beyond.
